newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX June electricity hits new highs on gas, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX June electricity hits new highs on gas, cash.

text.p: NYMEX June electricity futures climbed higher midday Wednesday, moving to new life-of-contract highs on rising physical power prices in the western U.S. and a rebound in the natural gas market.
Cash power values especially in the Southwest continued to strengthen on high air-conditioning demand due to hot weather in the interior section of the region.
"It's the heat combined with the gas," said a West Coast electricity dealer, referring to the factors behind the rally.
NYMEX June Henry Hub futures were up 5.1 cents at $2.240 per million British thermal units.
June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures rose 63 cents to $17.65 a megawatt hour (MWh) after setting a new contract high at $18.00.
July COB climbed 55 cents at $18.90. Other COB months were five to 10 cents higher.
June Palo Verde (PV) futures jumped 80 cents to $23.90 after posting a new contract at $24.20.
July PV gained 65 cents to $26.25. Deferred PV contracts were up 40 to 75 cents.
Firm, peak power prices at COB for Thursday firmed to $18.50-21.00 a MWh from yesterday's $17.75-18.75, while those at PV rocketed to $33.00-36.00 a MWh from yesterday's $26.50-28.50.

Overnight increase in capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission lines was shrugged off by the market. Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) boosted capacity on the Intertie to 7,200 megawatts (MW) from 6,250 MW at midnight.
"It was no big surprise. Now it's here. It's a non-event," said a Houston futures trader.
Most of the Southwest was forecast to see dry and warmer-than-normal spring temperatures through next week. The California coast was called to see seasonal readings in the high-60s to low-80s.
A warm, dry weather system was expected to stay over the Northwest into next week with well-above normal readings likely in the southern region.
At Tuesday's settlement, COB open interest ended up 169 contracts at 5,569, and PV open interest finished unchanged at 6,330.
